Subject: [ALERT] sustained tail latency increase - affected customers (FinWell)

Karthik / Lauren / Marcus —

Monitoring flagged a sustained increase in p99 tail latency for our text-generation route in us-west-2 starting ~15:45 PDT. Stack traces look normal, but request queueing increased on a subset of dedicated hosts (pool-ded-4). Impact: elevated token latency for customers on dedicated capacity; FinWell reported timeouts for batch inference jobs.

Quick summary:
- Start: 2026-08-25 15:45 PDT
- Peak p99 increase: from 420ms -> 2.2s
- Throughput: total RPS stable but per-host queuing spiked ~3x
- Suspected cause: uneven task distribution after a scale event + degraded NVLink perf on 2/8 hosts (observed NIC counters)

Immediate asks:
1) Marcus / infra: can you confirm NVLink/host health and whether autoscaler mis-routed traffic?
2) Lauren / product: need a short customer-facing note (1-2 paragraphs) to share with affected accounts — we should include workaround and ETA for fix.
3) Karthik / AE: please loop FinWell and set expectations; they are on a renewal cadence next month.

I opened PERF-4821 and attached a brief graph (redwood_latency_graph_20260826.png). Will follow up with deeper traces.

—Dylan

Quick update: I confirmed two host NICs exhibiting degraded throughput; NVLink metrics look fishy on those nodes. We've quarantined the two hosts from the pool and rebalanced traffic — that reduced queueing but p99 is still ~1.1s for some long-sequence requests.

Fallback options we can implement in the next 20-30 minutes:
- Route FinWell and other affected dedicated customers to pool-ded-2 (warm, lower load) — low risk, brief config change.
- Apply model variant downgrade (same family, int8 quantized) for latency-sensitive endpoints — measurable latency improvement but small delta in output distribution; requires opt-in per-customer if contract dictates.

If you want immediate customer mitigation, routing to pool-ded-2 is the fastest with minimal behavioral change. I'll keep PERF-4821 updated and post trace artifacts in the Drive link.

Subject: Update on elevated latency affecting jobs in us-west-2

Hi Alex —

We wanted to let you know about an elevated latency issue that affected several dedicated workloads in us-west-2 yesterday. Our SRE team detected queuing on a subset of hosts during a scaling event which temporarily increased the p99 for some generation and batch jobs.

What we did: we quarantined the impacted hosts and rebalanced traffic to healthy pools. As an immediate mitigation, we routed affected workloads to an alternate dedicated pool which reduced queueing and restored most customers to expected latency levels.

What this means for you: You may have seen timeouts or slower response for a small number of long-sequence requests between 15:40–16:10 PDT on Aug 25. No data was exposed and there is no action required from your side.

Next steps: our infra engineers are completing a post-mortem and we'll share a summary and any follow-up mitigations (including autoscaler tuning and host remediation) by EOD Friday. We've also opened JIRA PERF-4821 for tracking.

If you'd like a sync to talk through the impact on your specific workloads, I can set aside 30 minutes today.

Thanks for your patience —
Karthik
